title: Horizontal Drain Fittings: Sanitary Tee vs. Combination Wye
description: Using a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that leads to frequent clogs. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. On horizontal runs, the sweep of a sanitary tee is too short, slowing down liquid velocity and allowing solids to settle. Instead, code requires a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye fitting. This proper directional change maintains flow velocity and prevents waste buildup inside the drainage line.

Horizontal Drain Fittings: Sanitary Tee vs. Combination Wye

Using a standard sanitary tee on a horizontal-to-horizontal drainage run is a common installation mistake that leads to frequent clogs. Sanitary tees are designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow. On horizontal runs, the sweep of a sanitary tee is too short, slowing down liquid velocity and allowing solids to settle. Instead, code requires a combination wye and eighth bend or a long-sweep wye fitting. This proper directional change maintains flow velocity and prevents waste buildup inside the drainage line.
